verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES. No blocking contradiction with the story, design/rules.md or the author's source, and every AC has an implementable path. But the plan as written fails its own gates or leaves ACs unprovable in 6 places (all marked major below): (1) the older-scenario regression list is wrong in both directions (fuel_cans missing, units_showcase wrongly listed, whole-file allowances hide regressions); (2) the UnitChoice slot restructure breaks the NameLabel path used by src and by the retained choice scenario; (3) the HUD reads carrier_type_index() == -1 before begin() and GDScript [-1] silently returns the last element (measured); (4) there is no way to inject a Token fixture before begin() runs, nor to count the 'one error' of a refusal; (5) stock/type data validation misses unknown ids, duplicate ids and a second carrier type; (6) the cursor rule is under-specified. Open point 12a is settled by reading: every destruction source runs before the MatchController inside one physics frame (priorities/tree order cited in the issues), and the retained destruction baseline already shows two Self-destructs landing on one tick ('both at once: destroyed at tick 2417/2417', baseline-out/split-destruction.txt). S0 as applied in the working tree is clean on the silent-break checks I ran (Base node_paths and node names renamed together in base.tscn and compound_base.tscn, %FlagStatusLabel plus the four string lookups renamed, layer 4 renamed and read by nothing, no canister identifier left except protected story-004 file-name citations and the Fuel Can's 'kanister' quote, and no clash of Flag, FlagRules, FlagStatus or TokenLedger with ClassDB on 4.7.2 or with the 235 cached script classes). Line numbers below are HEAD 8e09d55 (the snap-head copy); the repo working tree is already post-S0, so lines there have moved. Probes: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tomas-kunzo-projects-ronin-ya-wasteland-fire/a0bbb76e-4a11-49a3-9a86-8984abd2268d/scratchpad/dev-story-008/design-critic/probe1/.
source_reading: Source text read in both languages (design/source/wasteland-fire-artifact-2026-10-01.sk.txt lines 34-42 and the .en.md lines 34-42 agree, no difference in meaning on these lines). The author says: each player has a stock of tokens per vehicle type, e.g. motorbike 5, buggy 3, truck 2, gyrocopter 2, counts set by the map and each map may differ ('Pocty urcuje mapa, kazda moze mat ine'); at the start and after every destruction the player picks any vehicle 'zo zvysnej zasoby' (from the remaining stock) and appears in the garage, and the game runs on meanwhile; a destroyed vehicle = minus 1 token of that type; only the motorbike carries the flag; the game ends when you bring the enemy flag home (win) or 'pridees o poslednu motorku' (you lose your last motorbike). The source says NOTHING about a HUD or any on-screen count, Self-destruct, a respawn delay, choosing during the countdown, a double loss, a Round-over screen, or different stocks per Player: those are conversation decisions or readings, and rules.md labels them as such (lines 11-17, 55-61). rules.md and the story read the source right: the Token is taken at the destruction ('zniceneho vozidlo = minus 1 token'), not at the spawn; the loss is the destruction that leaves the Motorbike stock at 0 (the only workable meaning of 'last motorbike', since each Player has exactly one Unit in play, so it can only refer to the stock; and Token-at-spawn would give the same loss event, so the reading is not fragile); 'a Map gives every Player at least 1 Motorbike Token' is the guard that makes both the carry and the loss possible; Self-destruct costing a Token and the choice during the countdown are decided 2026-10-01. design.txt follows rules.md and the story on every point I checked. Its deviations are small: (a) section 5 puts the 0-Token refusal in GarageQueue._try_respawn() while the story's note says _spawn() refuses it; (b) it generalises 'the Motorbike' to 'the types with can_carry', which the story invites; (c) the HUD shows only the carrier type's count (story AC-6 says 'at least'); (d) two counts are not stated anywhere in rules.md and must be recorded: the HUD count includes the Unit in play (the Token is not yet subtracted), and a Player who Self-destructs their last Motorbike forfeits the Round (rules.md line 57 'costs a Token like any destruction' plus line 61 make that the consequence). One CONTEXT.md wording clashes with the rule: the Token entry says 'One spawn of one Unit type', which reads as spent at the spawn.

issues.where: Design section 10 (older scenarios whose output changes) and section 1 (31 baselines byte-identical); tools/dev08.py:34-41 STRICT/SOFT lists
issues.problem: The list of retained scenarios affected by the UI change is wrong in both directions. (a) fuel_cans is STRICT and prints the status label rectangle twice, 'status=16,46-624,76' (fuel_cans.gd:358 reads rect_of.call("CanisterStatusLabel"); baseline-out/split-fuel_cans.txt line 31). Narrowing FlagStatusLabel (design section 8) changes it, and the design does not list fuel_cans, so regress fails it. (b) units_showcase prints only Unit type/position/hp/alive and Round events (units_showcase.gd:186-189), no HUD or panel geometry, so nothing in it can legitimately change; allowing it hides a regression in the cursor/choice flow it walks with real keys. (c) choice changes only in its panel=(x,y wxh) readings (baseline: choosing 40,562 560x142; ready 40,596 560x108; pre-layout start 40,1122 560x142); slots=[...], marks, tick counts, 'cursor_moves=10' and 'chosen=6 spawned=6 destroyed=3' must stay byte-identical. (d) hud changes three ways: the status label width, the new Tokens element in the fits_view line, and, from the rename alone, 'widest_text=349 of 608 px'. Measured on 4.7.2 with the default theme font at 20 px (reproduces the baseline 349): 'You carry the enemy Flag' 244 px, 'Your Flag is at home' 196, 'Your Flag is away' 166; 'Motorbike Tokens: 5' 197, '...: 99' 209. So section 1's claim that all 31 outputs stay identical after map_text is false for hud. (e) dev08.py:41 makes canister_run, hud, round_over and canister_showcase SOFT (RESULT ok only); only hud needs that, the others should compare byte-for-byte after map_text (NOT DETERMINED whether they match; I did not run them).
issues.fix: List fuel_cans, choice and hud as the changed ones and drop units_showcase. Replace whole-file allowances in allowed-diffs.json by normalizers in dev08 regress that mask only: panel=(...) in choice, status=... in fuel_cans, the status/Tokens rects and widest_text in hud. Every other byte of those outputs is then still compared. Promote canister_run (flag_run), round_over and canister_showcase (flag_showcase) to STRICT if they match after map_text. State the exact expected values (244/196/166 px; narrowed width) in the evidence doc.

issues.where: Design section 7 (UnitChoice CountLabel in SlotTemplate); src/ui/hud/unit_choice.gd:314; tools/evidence/split_screen/choice.gd:312-320; unit_choice.tscn:100-114
issues.problem: A PanelContainer lays every child into the same rectangle, so a CountLabel beside NameLabel needs a container (a VBox) between them. That moves NameLabel off the slot's direct children and breaks two string paths: unit_choice.gd:314 panel.get_node(^"NameLabel") and the retained choice.gd:320 slot.get_node(^"NameLabel") (reads the NameLabel text of each Slots child to compare with the display names). The design never mentions it; choice would error mid-coroutine (watchdog fail), not merely differ. Related traps: the label colours are scene-stored theme overrides, so remove_theme_color_override() when un-dimming falls back to the theme's default grey, not the scene's white; and an export equal to its script default is not written to a saved scene (the project's own note at unit_choice.gd:120-125), so a dim colour default must not equal the stored value.
issues.fix: Fix the new relative path now (for example Lines/NameLabel and Lines/CountLabel), fetch both by relative path in _rebuild_slots() (never % names: duplicate() of the template does not give the copies a registrable owner), edit choice.gd:320 and name it as a scenario edit. Keep NameLabel.text == tr(display_name) so choice.gd:333 still compares equal. Store normal and dim font colours as data and set one of them explicitly on every refresh. Panel growth is arithmetic-safe (baseline panel top 562 / countdown text bottom 404 / HUD band bottom 84) but the new height is NOT DETERMINED: measure it.

issues.where: Design section 8 and open point 12c; src/ui/hud/player_hud.gd:162-182; split_screen.gd:139
issues.problem: Open point 12c says carrier_type_index() == -1 'cannot happen after begin()'s validation'. It happens before begin(): every child's _ready() runs before SplitScreen._ready(), so PlayerHud._ready() (where section 8 wants a first re-read) runs while the ledger is empty, carrier_type_index() is -1 and tokens_left() is 0. It also persists when begin() refuses a stock. GDScript treats -1 as 'last element' (measured on 4.7.2: names[-1] returned 'Gyrocopter', counts[-1] returned the last count), so unit_types()[carrier_type_index()] would paint 'Gyrocopter Tokens: 0'. The same trap exists in any ledger accessor that range-checks only the upper bound.
issues.fix: The HUD must not index with a negative result: hide or blank the label until round_started (do not re-read in _ready()), or compute the carrier index from rules.unit_types so it is valid before begin() and still hide the label while the Round has not begun. Define tokens_left()/can_choose() with 0 <= type_index < size and 0 <= player < players, and add the matrix check for -1, size, and a Player outside the Round.

issues.where: Design section 10 (fixtures made in code, scenarios registered) vs tools/evidence/split_screen_harness.gd:292-318; AC-1 'one error that names it'; AC-9
issues.problem: The harness instances the launch scene and add_child()s it (begin() runs inside) before any scenario's run() exists (harness lines 311-318, 326-341), so a fixture stock built inside run() reaches nothing; and a second begin() is refused first by the _has_begun check (match_controller.gd:225). The design does not say how a fixture reaches begin() or how 'exactly one error' is observed. Fixtures are not optional: the matrix needs the real Map 01 stock, a one-Motorbike stock, a mixed stock and a 99 stock, and one process has one stock. Also measured: a literal assigned to a Dictionary[StringName,int] property works, an untyped Dictionary variable assigned to it is a runtime SCRIPT ERROR, and a reference to stock.counts writes through to the shared resource (alias[k]=9 changed the source), which is the realistic form of the 'shared TokenStock written to' defect.
issues.fix: Add a runner hook like OWN_CHOICE/WATCHDOG_SECONDS (script.get_script_constant_map()): a scenario constant (for example TOKEN_FIXTURE) that the runner turns into a fresh TokenStock (per-key assignment stock.counts[id] = n) on split.field.token_stock before add_child(split); one scenario family per fixture. Test refusals on a throwaway MatchController.new() (shared rules, the live Units/Bases/cameras) with an OS.add_logger(Logger subclass) counting _log_error: measured on 4.7.2, push_error arrives as rationale text and push_warning with error_type ERROR_TYPE_WARNING. Do AC-4 on the real stock (five lockstep Self-destructs) so no fixture is needed there.

issues.where: Design section 2/3 (begin() validation, first_problem); src/gameplay/maps/token_stock.gd:32-39; src/gameplay/units/unit_stats.gd:263-270
issues.problem: Validation covers null stock, negative count and 'no Token for the carrier', but not: (a) a stock key that matches no unit type (a typo such as &"gyrocopte" silently makes that type unavailable all Round; count_of() hides it by design); (b) two unit_types with the same type_id, or an empty one (UnitStats.first_problem() does not check type_id; the damage matrix and the stock are keyed by it), which would give two index slots one pool or none; (c) two types with can_carry: carrier_type_index() is 'the first', the HUD shows that one, but has_lost() sums all carriers, so the HUD can read 0 while the Player has not lost. 'No Token for any type that can carry' is also ambiguous for that case.
issues.fix: begin() refuses with one error each: an unknown stock key (names it), a duplicate or empty type_id among unit_types, and a count of carrier types other than exactly one (or make the HUD show carry_total; pick one and state it in the class doc). Cover the pure parts (TokenLedger.start/take/has_lost/first_problem) in gdUnit4 under tests/unit/match/ if tests are not waived, because they need no scene.

issues.where: Design section 6 (PlayerChoiceInput) and section 7 (mark rules); AC-3; player_choice_input.gd:87-100; unit_choice.gd:320-323
issues.problem: The cursor rule leaves open: (a) what 'starts choosing' is (unit_destroyed/round_started signals, or a poll inside _physics_process) and the order against the key reads in the same function: if the snap comes after the fire read, a press on the first choosing tick is refused (0-count) and swallowed; (b) whether cursor_moved is emitted when a steer key cannot move the cursor (one selectable type) or the snap changes nothing; choice.gd counts the emits (cursor_moves=10, 7 in the dance); (c) a search written as a loop over 'next type with Tokens' never ends when no type has Tokens, which is reachable for one tick: the last Motorbike destroyed while every other type is at 0 (the take happens before unit_destroyed, the loss check later in the same controller tick; listeners run in between); (d) UnitChoice._mark_slot() currently marks the cursor slot regardless, so between the destruction tick and PlayerChoiceInput's next tick (it runs at priority -1, before the Units) the panel would mark a dimmed 0-count slot unless the mark rule itself excludes it.
issues.fix: Specify: snap inside _physics_process right after the is_choosing guard and before any key read (and also on round_started for data whose first type is empty), search bounded to unit_types.size() steps with 'leave the cursor' as the all-zero result, cursor_moved only when the index changed, and _mark_slot() never marks a slot whose count is 0 whatever the cursor says. Keep the emit count identical for the all-positive (99) case so choice stays byte-identical.

issues.where: Design section 3/4 (ledger counts[player][i] by index, take by type_id lookup); garage_queue.gd:384; destruction.gd:206-211
issues.problem: The ledger is indexed by position but the garage re-reads rules.unit_types live and destruction.gd already swaps controller.rules for a duplicate at runtime (the duplicate shares the order, so it works today). A swap with another order or length would charge the wrong type and let choose() pass or refuse the wrong index.
issues.fix: Key the ledger by type_id (Dictionary[StringName,int] per Player) and convert the live index to an id at the call; take() then needs no lookup and 'destroyed type not in the data' is a missing key.

issues.where: Design section 5 (GarageQueue._try_respawn refuses a 0-Token choice); story note says _spawn(); ui reads unit_chosen only
issues.problem: The branch is unreachable (a Player with no Unit in play cannot lose a Token, and choose() already refuses), so no scenario can exercise it; if it ever ran, it clears the choice without a signal, so UnitChoice would keep showing 'X ready' (it only learns from unit_chosen/unit_spawned/unit_destroyed/round_started/cursor_moved, unit_choice.gd:182-187). It also adds lines to a file already past the doc-size concerns (TD-010).
issues.fix: Drop it, or keep a push_error with no state change and say it is a guard for a bug; do not clear the choice silently.

issues.where: AC-8 'every retained scenario under tools/evidence/ is re-run'; dev08.py:34-41
issues.problem: The regress list is the 31 headless baselines (27 STRICT, 4 SOFT). Not covered: fps and map_fps (windowed frame-rate tools, registered in the harness) and tools/evidence/input_ghosting_check. AC-8 as written includes them.

issues.problem: NO_WINNER (-1) now means both 'Round running' and 'Round over, nobody won'; only is_round_over() tells them apart. issues.where: Design section 4 'a delivery that already set OVER wins' and open point 12a
issues.problem: Settled by reading, no change needed except the test list: every destruction source runs before the controller in a physics frame. Self-destruct and debug damage: PlayerMatchInput priority = unit - 1 = -1 (player_match_input.gd:91); Fuel crash: Unit._burn_fuel inside Unit._physics_process (unit.gd:641) at priority 0 in World; Shots: weapon.gd:113 adds them under the Unit's parent (World) and their tick is priority 0, tree order before the MatchController, which has default priority 0 and sits after World and Views (split_screen.tscn:212-215). The delivery-versus-loss branch cannot name two different winners: a Carrier that is alive for the delivery cannot have spent its last Motorbike Token (the Token is taken at the destruction, and may_act() excludes a destroyed Player), so that precedence line is a dead branch.

issues.problem: fits_view iterates every HUD child, so the new label is measured automatically, but only for its current text (the one-digit '5' or whatever LEGACY 99 gives), and only the status label gets 'every stored text' widths. Overflow at 2-3 digits or a longer display_name would not be seen; the Team edge (8,8)-(632,84) staying unchanged is not asserted.
issues.fix: Add the worst case of the Tokens label (count 99 and 100, longest display_name in unit_types) to the width test, assert its rect does not intersect the status label or the bars, and assert the union of the HUD children is still (16,16)-(624,76).

issues.where: AC-9 'no count is a constant in code' vs section 10 LEGACY_TOKEN_COUNT = 99
issues.problem: The 99 is a constant in tools/, which is test data, but AC-9 as worded does not say so; and older showcase output will show 'x99' counts.
issues.fix: State AC-9's scope as src/ (the game), add a lint that finds no integer Token literal in src/gameplay/match and src/ui/hud other than 0/1 comparisons, and note that the older retained frames are not regenerated.

missing_cases: Stock key that matches no unit type (typo): begin() refuses with one error naming the key; today it is silently ignored and the type is simply unavailable.
Two unit_types with the same or an empty type_id: begin() refuses (stock, damage matrix and the ledger are keyed by it).
Two types with can_carry: refuse (exactly one carrier type) or make HUD and has_lost() use the same number; today the HUD shows the first carrier, the loss sums all.
HUD and panels before begin() and after a refused begin(): label hidden or empty, panels hidden, no read through index -1 (measured: [-1] is the last element).

A Player whose only Tokens are Motorbikes: the other three slots dim, the cursor sits on the Motorbike, A and D leave it there (and say whether cursor_moved fires), fire chooses the Motorbike and the Unit appears as usual.

No type has Tokens for the one tick between the take and the loss check (last Motorbike destroyed with every other type at 0): bounded cursor search, no hang, no error, panel hidden by round_over in the same tick.

Fire pressed on the first choosing tick while the cursor rests on the type just exhausted: the cursor snaps before the key read and the press confirms the type the panel shows (or is refused visibly); it must not be swallowed.

Last Motorbike destroyed while carrying the enemy Flag: flag_dropped before unit_destroyed, Token 0, round_over with the other Player as winner; after R both Flags AT_HOME on their seats and both statuses 'at home'.

Double loss then R at once: winner_index() is -1 and is_round_over() true before, -1 and false after; both stocks full; the Round-over screen hidden; no round_over on the first tick after the restart.
Restart after each kind of end (delivery, single loss, double loss): both stocks refilled including the winner's, un-dimmed slots back to the scene's normal style and white font, HUD labels full.
Self-destruct pressed while benched or already destroyed, and a lethal Shot plus Self-destruct on the same tick: at most one Token (destroy() and note_destroyed() are idempotent; assert it).
P2's Self-destruct one tick after P1's fatal tick: ignored (tree paused), P2's stock unchanged, P2 wins; this is the near-miss that separates 'same tick' from 'close ticks'.
Destroyed Unit whose type_id is not in unit_types (a tool spawned it with Unit.spawn()): one warning, no Token taken, never a loss.

controller.rules replaced at runtime with another unit_types order or length (destruction.gd:206-211 swaps it today): charge and choose must stay correct (key the ledger by type_id) or the swap is refused.
A Map that gives a non-carrier type 0 from the start, including the first type of the data: dim from the first frame, the cursor starts on the first available type.
Both Players choosing on the same tick with different stocks: independent accept/refuse, each Unit keeps the 3-tick bench settle.
Counts of 100 or more (three digits) in HUD and slot: still one line inside the 560 px panel and the HUD row (undefined today; the design only promises 99).

Stock edited in the shared .tres between begin and restart: restart() copies from the held stock reference, so a runtime edit would leak in; state that the resource is read-only and never copied by alias.
A Player who loses while the other Player's Flag lies dropped far away: nothing is picked up after round_over (tree paused) and R reseats both; no stale carrier state in FlagRules.
The HUD count includes the Unit in play: 5 while the first Motorbike drives, 4 after its destruction; a Player on their last Motorbike reads 1 (record this in rules.md).
test_matrix: T01 ac1_start_from_data: Map 01 real stock, after the first round_started: for p in {0,1} and every type i, tokens_left(p,i) == field.token_stock.count_of(unit_types[i].type_id) (5,3,2,2 read from the resource, not typed) and the HUD reads the Motorbike line with 5; repeat with a fixture {motorbike 2, buggy 0, truck 7, gyrocopter 1} -> equals the fixture. Kills: hardcoded 5/3/2/2, one Player only, wrong index order, counts not from data (also AC-9).

Kills: ledger holding stock.counts by reference (measured: a Dictionary[StringName,int] alias writes through), writing back to the stock or UnitStats.
